label: Food Insecure Population
contestNote: UPDATED Jul 14, 2026: UN Humanitarian Coordinator George Conway confirmed a 'real and credible risk of famine' in Burhakaba District (Bay Region) — the first district-level famine-risk confirmation of the crisis. WFP (Jun 28) reaching only 450,000 people (down from 2.2M in early 2025) as 2M enter IPC Phase 4 Emergency (double the prior year); 1.9M children face acute malnutrition; 76% of the IPC-4 population has no assistance pipeline through August. Nationally, 570,000+ need water assistance and 400,730 children face acute malnutrition (97,150 severe). HRP still only 15.2% funded as of Jul 14; over 500 health/nutrition facilities closed for lack of funds; water-trucking costs more than doubled in some areas.
delta: Burhakaba famine risk CONFIRMED (Jul 14) — first district-level famine-risk finding of the crisis; HRP still 15.2% funded
deltaNote: UN (Jul 14, 2026): 'The humanitarian context in Somalia is worsening faster than we originally projected... without immediate and sustained support from donors, the diaspora and the private sector, we risk a preventable catastrophe.' Somalia Humanitarian Fund allocated $4.7M to Burhakaba (incl. $2M reserve). No confirmed WFP full operational shutdown, but reach has fallen to roughly 1-in-5 of the early-2025 caseload.

label: AUSSOM Authorized Strength
source: UNSC Resolution 2809 / AU / ChimpReports Jul 1, 2026 / Reuters Sep 18, 2026
delta: US grants UN 12-month drawdown window (from Jan 2027) instead of immediate Dec 31, 2026 cutoff
deltaNote: In a July 1, 2026 letter to the African Union, the US said it will not support UNSOS — AUSSOM's logistics backbone (fuel, medevac, food, engineering, COE reimbursement) — beyond Dec 31, 2026, and will oppose any UNSC renewal including UNSOS support. Cites Somalia's failure to take ownership of security despite ~$2B in UNSOS support plus $1.6B bilateral aid over a decade. AU Commission convened an emergency meeting; a senior African diplomat called the decision 'irreversible.' UPDATED Aug 25-26, 2026 (Radio Dalsan / WardheerNews): the drawdown moved from planning to execution — at least 10 civilian AU-UN Information Support Team staff received termination notices effective Sep 10, and UNSOS began auctioning vehicles, generators, medical supplies and other equipment. UPDATED Sep 18, 2026 (Reuters/US News, CNBC Africa): the US told the UN in a diplomatic note it is willing to support a 12-month drawdown followed by liquidation of UNSOS, starting January 2027, rather than the earlier all-at-once Dec 31, 2026 cutoff; final timelines to be set during December UNSC deliberations. Analyst Samira Gaid warned UNSOS's shutdown could still trigger AUSSOM's collapse; Prof. Afyare Elmi called AUSSOM 'a key pillar of Somalia's state,' with its loss risking 'a real risk of state fragmentation.' Defence Minister Fiqi countered publicly on Sep 20 that Al-Shabaab 'cannot capture even a single village' even if AUSSOM leaves. UNTMIS separately remains on track to complete transition to a standard UN country team by Oct 31, 2026. Roughly 11,862 uniformed personnel still depend on UNSOS for supply and shelter. Separately, funding and logistical hurdles have delayed deployment of Egyptian troop reinforcements to AUSSOM.

contestNote: At least 83 confirmed strikes in Somalia by September 17, 2026, after AFRICOM disclosed the Sep 14 strike near Saacow, Middle Juba, and a Sep 17 strike on a weapons warehouse in the Sanaag region (80mi SW of Bosaso) — keeping 2026 on pace to approach or exceed 2025's record total of roughly 124-126 strikes. AFRICOM no longer discloses civilian harm assessments or unit/asset details for operational security.

Pace remains the highest on record for Somalia.

label: Piracy Hostages (Simultaneous, 2026)
source: UnHerd Aug 10, 2026 / AP Aug 20-22, 2026 / CTV News, Express Tribune Sep 11-12, 2026 / IMO
contestNote: The Sward (hijacked off Garacad Apr 26, 2026; 17 crew — 15 Syrian, 2 Indian) was released around Sep 11, 2026 after a ransom was paid, per security sources cited by CTV News and the Express Tribune — the first resolved case of Somalia's 2026 piracy resurgence. That leaves an estimated 50+ hostages across 5+ vessels still held, including Honour 25 (17 crew, £3M ransom demand outstanding), MT Eureka (12 crew, $10M demand), the Cameroon-flagged Lutuf (crew reported safe) and the Eritrean-flagged Sibu 1/Seamull (20 crew, 16 Indian). No comprehensive re-count has been re-published by IMO/EU NAVFOR since Sibu 1's Aug 20 hijacking, so the figure remains an estimate net of the Sward's release.
delta: First hostage release of 2026: Sword freed near Garacad (Sep 11) after ransom paid
deltaNote: Pirates reportedly used the Sward as a mothership to help seize at least two other vessels during its four-month captivity before releasing it. No other held vessel has seen a ransom paid or hostages released as of Sep 13.
